o: Solomon shows that all human things are vain.
Man's toil and want of satisfaction.
The vexation in pursuit of knowledge.
bg: ecclesiastes
The Greek rendering of the Hebrew Koheleth, which means "Preacher." The old and traditional view of the authorship of this book attributes it to Solomon.
ch.s: This chapter covers: Solomon shows that all human things are vain (vv. 1–3); Man's toil and want of satisfaction (vv. 4–8); There is nothing new (vv. 9–11); The vexation in pursuit of knowledge (vv. 12–18). People named: David. Places: Jerusalem.
ch.mh: Much is to be learned by comparing one part of Scripture with another.
q: Read verses 1–3 (Solomon shows that all human things are vain). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 4–8 (Man's toil and want of satisfaction), what do you learn about wisdom?
Verse 2 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Psalms 144:4. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does David’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of the holy spirit in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Ecclesiastes?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us learn to hate and fear sin, the cause of all this vanity and misery; to value Christ; to seek rest in the knowledge, love, and service of the Saviour.
ch.a: Before a decision this week, pause and ask what this chapter would counsel.
